reference.source: Green's Operative Hand Surgery / Campbell's Operative Orthopaedics
clinicalPearls: Despite its name it is not a true neoplasm but a perineural fibrosis of a common plantar digital nerve
The third web space, between the third and fourth metatarsal heads, is most commonly affected, followed by the second web space
Patients describe burning plantar forefoot pain radiating into the adjacent toes and often the sensation of a pebble or lump within the shoe
Symptoms are aggravated by tight or high-heeled footwear and relieved by removing the shoe and massaging the foot
The Mulder click is a palpable and sometimes audible click produced by mediolateral compression of the forefoot combined with dorsoplantar pressure over the web space
There is tenderness in the affected web space and sensory disturbance in the contiguous borders of the involved toes
The condition is markedly more common in women, in keeping with the association with constrictive footwear
Generic management includes footwear modification and metatarsal pads or orthoses, corticosteroid injection, and surgical excision or neurolysis for refractory cases
reference.pathophysiology: A Morton neuroma is a mechanically induced degenerative process of a common plantar interdigital nerve rather than a genuine tumour. The nerve is irritated where it passes beneath the deep transverse intermetatarsal ligament, and the third web space is especially vulnerable where medial and lateral plantar nerve contributions converge. Repetitive dorsiflexion in narrow footwear causes chronic compression and traction, leading to perineural fibrosis, endoneurial oedema and thickening of the nerve, which generate the characteristic neuritic pain.
additionalDifferentials: Metatarsophalangeal joint synovitis or plantar plate instability, particularly of the second toe
Freiberg disease (osteochondrosis of a metatarsal head)
Tarsal tunnel syndrome or a more proximal plantar nerve entrapment
additionalInvestigations: Clinical examination including the Mulder click and web space compression test
Ultrasound as the usual first-line imaging to confirm and size the lesion
MRI when ultrasound is equivocal or other pathology is suspected
Weightbearing plain radiographs to exclude a bony cause such as stress fracture or Freiberg disease
A diagnostic local anaesthetic injection into the web space to confirm the pain source
redFlags: Features suggesting a soft-tissue tumour rather than an interdigital neuroma
Bilateral or multiple lesions prompting consideration of an alternative diagnosis
A progressive neurological deficit pointing to a more proximal cause
reference.prognosis: Many patients improve with footwear modification and injection, and surgical excision gives good relief, though it carries a risk of a recurrent stump neuroma and a permanent patch of sensory loss between the toes.
pitfalls: Attributing pain to a neuroma when the true source is metatarsophalangeal joint synovitis or plantar plate instability
A painful stump neuroma developing after excision
Repeated corticosteroid injection causing plantar fat atrophy or plantar plate attenuation
